svg.title: School records before the event
svg.desc: School records before the event; 2005 comparison schools: not estimable: first panel boundary; 2005 schools that later lost provision: not estimable: first panel boundary; 2006 comparison schools: 96.5 %; 2006 schools that later lost provision: 92.0 %; 2007 comparison schools: 96.6 %; 2007 schools that later lost provision: 92.1 %; 2008 comparison schools: 96.5 %; 2008 schools that later lost provision: 96.4 %; 2009 comparison schools: 97.0 %; 2009 schools that later lost provision: 88.8 %; 2010 comparison schools: 98.0 %; 2010 schools that later lost provision: 97.6 %; 2011 comparison schools: 97.8 %; 2011 schools that later lost provision: 95.6 %; 2012 comparison schools: 97.8 %; 2012 schools that later lost provision: 95.5 %; 2013 comparison schools: withheld to prevent small-group disclosure when tables are combined; 2013 schools that later lost provision: 95.5 %; 2014 comparison schools: withheld to prevent small-group disclosure when tables are combined; 2014 schools that later lost provision: 94.8 %; 2015 comparison schools: 97.9 %; 2015 schools that later lost provision: 95.1 %. Students in school cohorts eligible for missing-record analysis; event cohorts 2005–2015 (historical definition). Observed rate of any school record between the second and first years before the event (G−2 to G−1), for schools that later lost provision and comparison schools; 0–100% scale. The student set differs from the primary analysis, which starts at G−1. Each rate pair describes different arms, not an individual trajectory. There is no adjustment, uncertainty interval, or test of anticipation or parallel trends. The 2005 cohort is not estimable at the first panel boundary; other unavailable rates are privacy suppressed. Some rates are withheld to prevent small-group disclosure when the two outcome tables are combined. The CSV retains every cohort and arm, disclosable student/school denominators and absence reasons; no identifiers or quantiles.
